title: Angular Momentum Quantization of a Charge-flux Composite: Quantum Electrodynamic Approach
abstract: The fractional angular momentum of a two-dimensional charge-flux composite is a well-established phenomenon usually derived from a semiclassical Hamiltonian. However, when the composite is treated as an isolated system in free two-dimensional space, the fundamental rotational and reflection symmetries of the $O(2)$ group demand that its total angular momentum is strictly quantized. We address this conceptual discrepancy by applying a full quantum electrodynamic (QED) approach combined with Noether's theorem. We demonstrate that the interaction between the charge and flux, mediated by the vacuum electromagnetic field, generates an intrinsic interaction angular momentum composed of both field momentum and hidden relativistic momentum. This gauge-invariant interaction angular momentum exactly compensates for the fractional part of the kinetic angular momentum. Consequently, the net angular momentum of the composite strictly follows the integer or half-integer quantization rule. Our formalism clarifies that the conventional fractional spin corresponds to the expectation value of the kinetic angular momentum within the perturbed QED ground state. It also elucidates why the standard classical field angular momentum definition fails to capture this in two dimensions, due to non-vanishing boundary terms.
summary: This paper resolves the paradox of angular momentum quantization for charge-flux composites by moving beyond semiclassical models to a full Quantum Electrodynamic treatment. The key finding is that the interaction with the vacuum electromagnetic field generates a compensating angular momentum term. This ensures the total angular momentum strictly adheres to integer or half-integer quantization, confirming the robustness of fundamental symmetries in 2D quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper resolves a conceptual conflict regarding the quantization of angular momentum for a two-dimensional charge-flux composite when treated as an isolated system in free space.
main_result: By employing a full Quantum Electrodynamic (QED) approach, the authors show that the interaction between the charge and flux generates an intrinsic angular momentum that exactly compensates for the fractional part of the kinetic angular momentum, restoring strict integer or half-integer quantization.
method: The analysis uses Noether's theorem applied to a full QED Lagrangian formalism, contrasting these results with insufficient semiclassical Hamiltonian treatments.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional charge-flux composite (anyon). The theoretical framework involves coupling the particle dynamics to the vacuum electromagnetic field via a QED Lagrangian.

main_assumptions: The semiclassical approach is insufficient; a full QED treatment incorporating vacuum field interactions is necessary to resolve the quantization paradox.

paper_structure: The paper contrasts semiclassical results (which fail) with a rigorous QED derivation using Noether's theorem. It identifies the compensating interaction term that restores quantization, while also noting the failure of standard field definitions in 2D due to boundary terms.
why_interesting: It provides a deep theoretical understanding of how gauge-invariant interactions (like those mediated by vacuum fields) can enforce fundamental symmetries and conservation laws on exotic quantum systems, which is relevant for understanding topological order or fractional statistics.

FIG. 2. A two-dimensional quantum analog of Feynman’s disk paradox. Two inﬁnitesimally close, counter-rotating loops carrying opposite charges generate the central magnetic ﬂux. A weak internal dissipative interaction, such as radiative damping, slows the loops to a complete rest. This allows the transfer of their mechanical angular momentum to the sur- rounding vacuum via the emission of photons (γ). Meanwhile, the adiabatic switching oﬀof the ﬂux induces an azimuthal electric ﬁeld that imparts an additional angular momentum of exactly +qΦ/2π to the external charge q via Faraday’s law of induction.
